dateline: Bamako / Kidal / Ménaka / Kompienbiga / Barsalogho / Labbezanga / Goubré — 2012–Present
heroHeadline: Bamako Siege Day 38: Mali Bans Motorcycles Nationwide; OCHA Warns 15.4M Face Lean Season; FLA Chief — 'Kidal Only the Beginning'
heroSubtitle: Day 38 of JNIM's declared 'total siege' of Bamako (announced April 28, 2026). On June 3, President Goïta signed Decree 2026-0312 banning motorcycles above 125cc outside urban centers — targeting JNIM's primary tactical mobility platform (Africanews, Washington Post, EWN); enforcement capacity across rural territory remains the critical uncertainty. UN/OCHA warned June 3 that 15.4M people across Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger face IPC Phase 3+ food crisis during the June–August lean season, with humanitarian funding at only 19% of the $3.7B request. FAMa and Africa Corps struck FLA logistics nodes in northern Mali on June 4 (Pravda Mali — single source, unconfirmed). ISS Africa (June 4) documented JNIM's trade corridor warfare costing Senegal's Dakar Port approximately 15 billion FCFA (~$26.5M) per month. A Bamako–Kayes highway landmine killed 8 passengers and wounded 42 on June 1 (Legit.ng, Sahara Reporters). ECOWAS mediator Lansana Kouyaté called June 3 for immediate AES cooperation frameworks. HRW reported June 5 that the US delivered $2.3M military equipment to Niger despite drone strikes killing 17 civilians. FLA chief Alghabass Ag Intalla stated publicly June 4: 'Kidal is only the beginning' — signaling FLA expansion intentions. Three key fronts: (1) BAMAKO BLOCKADE (Day 38): 3 of 6 roads cut; motorcycle ban decree in force; Africa Corps BMP-3 clearing burned trucks from northern highways; no renewed JNIM escalation in post-Eid window but structural blockade unchanged. (2) KIDAL FRONT: FLA retains city control; FAMa/Africa Corps aerial campaign continues; FLA logistics interdiction strikes June 4. (3) BURKINA FASO: Imam Mohamed Kindo remains detained without charges since May 26; Traoré junta faces continued domestic pressure following mosque closures and protester detentions.
